# gcore_waap_domain_firewall_rule (Resource)

WAAP firewall rules allow or block requests to a domain based on the client IP address or IP range.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "gcore_waap_domain_firewall_rule" "example_waap_domain_firewall_rule" {
  domain_id = 1
  action = {
    allow = {
      foo = "bar"
    }
    block = {
      action_duration = "12h"
      status_code = 403
    }
  }
  conditions = [{
    ip = {
      ip_address = "ip_address"
      negation = true
    }
    ip_range = {
      lower_bound = "lower_bound"
      upper_bound = "upper_bound"
      negation = true
    }
  }]
  enabled = true
  name = "Block foobar bot"
  description = "description"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `action` (Attributes) The action that the rule takes when triggered (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action))
- `conditions` (Attributes List) The condition required for the WAAP engine to trigger the rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions))
- `domain_id` (Number) The domain ID
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether or not the rule is enabled
- `name` (String) The name assigned to the rule

### Optional

- `description` (String) The description assigned to the rule

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The unique identifier of the rule

<a id="nestedatt--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action`

Optional:

- `allow` (Map of String) The WAAP allows the request
- `block` (Attributes) WAAP block action behavior could be configured with response status code and action duration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--block))

<a id="nestedatt--action--block"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.block`

Optional:

- `action_duration` (String) How long a rule's block action will apply to subsequent requests. Can be specified in seconds or by using a numeral followed by 's', 'm', 'h', or 'd' to represent time format (seconds, minutes, hours, or days). Empty time intervals are not allowed.
- `status_code` (Number) A custom HTTP status code that the WAAP returns if a rule blocks a request
Available values: 403, 405, 418, 429.



<a id="nestedatt--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions`

Optional:

- `ip` (Attributes) Match the incoming request against a single IP address (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--ip))
- `ip_range` (Attributes) Match the incoming request against an IP range (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions--ip_range))

<a id="nestedatt--conditions--ip"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions.ip`

Required:

- `ip_address` (String) A single IPv4 or IPv6 address

Optional:

- `negation` (Boolean) Whether or not to apply a boolean NOT operation to the rule's condition


<a id="nestedatt--conditions--ip_range"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions.ip_range`

Required:

- `lower_bound` (String) The lower bound IPv4 or IPv6 address to match against
- `upper_bound` (String) The upper bound IPv4 or IPv6 address to match against

Optional:

- `negation` (Boolean) Whether or not to apply a boolean NOT operation to the rule's condition

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import gcore_waap_domain_firewall_rule.example '<domain_id>/<rule_id>'
```
